new_jobs.description:
We’re ALTEN Technology USA, an engineering company helping clients bring groundbreaking ideas to life—from advancing space exploration and life-saving medical devices to building autonomous electric vehicles. With 3,000+ experts across North America, we partner with leading companies in aerospace, medical devices, robotics, automotive, commercial vehicles, EVs, rail, and more.
As part of the global ALTEN Group—57,000+ engineers in 30 countries—we deliver across the entire product development cycle, from consulting to full project outsourcing.
When you join ALTEN Technology USA, you’ll collaborate on some of the world’s toughest engineering challenges, supported by mentorship, career growth opportunities, and comprehensive benefits. We take pride in fostering a culture where employees feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow.
Workplace:
On-site, 5 days per week
Location:
San Francisco, CA (Dogpatch neighborhood) 
Salary:
$90,000-$105,000
We are seeking a Robotics Lab Technician to be the versatile builder at the center of our prototype lab. You'll move fluidly between precision assembly, wiring and electrical integration, system bring-up, and acceptance testing to take robots from a kit of parts to a validated, working system. You'll install software and read logs, bridging the gap between hardware and software during bring-up, and you’ll troubleshoot and solve integration issues during testing and validation. We're looking for someone careful with their hands, organized about documentation, and comfortable collaborating with mechanical, electrical, controls, and software engineers in a fast-iterating environment.
Key Job Responsibilities

    • Assemble electromechanical robotic systems and subsystems (actuators, gearboxes, sensors, vision systems, wiring harnesses, PCBAs) from mechanical drawings, schematics, and work instructions, following torque specs and assembly procedures.
    • Kit parts against the BOM, stage hardware and fixtures, and set up assembly jigs and alignment rigs for each build.
    • Build first articles from prototype kits, provide engineering with actionable build feedback (DFx), and execute rework and engineering change orders (ECOs) as designs iterate.
    • Fabricate, route, and terminate wiring harnesses to documented pinouts with proper strain relief, bend radius management, and cable routing for moving assemblies.
    • Perform pre-power-on electrical verification (continuity, pinout, insulation, polarity) and board-level integration under ESD discipline.
    • Maintain build records, travelers, inspection checklists, and non-conformance reports (NCRs) ensuring full traceability. Redline and improve work instructions with each build.
    • Bring up newly built assemblies, verify actuator and sensor function, and run acceptance testing and performance characterization using standard and custom test equipment.
    • Use git and the Linux command line to install, configure, and run test and calibration software on robots; track software versions across the fleet.
    • Read logs and source code well enough to localize problems and provide engineering with actionable triage reports.
    • Collaborate with engineering to isolate integration issues, narrow root cause across mechanical, electrical, and software domains, and drive corrective actions into work instructions.
    • Keep the lab safe, organized, and ESD-compliant; track tooling, consumables, and inventory.
    • Drive continuous improvement and support prototype-to-production transitions by developing SOPs, assembly aids, and training materials.

Required Qualifications

    • 3-5+ years of hands-on experience assembling and testing electromechanical systems such as robotics hardware, precision mechatronic assemblies, aerospace/automotive hardware, or electronics assembly in a lab, prototype, or manufacturing environment.
    • Able to read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and written work instructions to build and test complex hardware.
    • Proficient with hand and torque tools, basic crimping and soldering, and steady work with small fasteners and connectors.
    • Demonstrated ability to perform functional and acceptance testing using standard test equipment such as multimeters, oscilloscopes, and power supplies.
    • Experience performing quality inspections and maintaining detailed build records, including assembly travelers, inspection checklists, and non-conformance documentation.
    • Comfortable at a Linux command line running scripts, and willing to grow those skills.
    • Knowledge of ESD handling procedures and lab safety protocols for working with high-voltage electronics and heavy mechanical assemblies.
    • Clear communication, careful record-keeping, and safe work habits.

Preferred Qualifications

    • Associate's degree or technical certification in Electronics Technology, Mechatronics, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent hands-on experience.
    • Experience assembling and testing robotic systems with high degrees of freedom, including familiarity with actuators, force/torque sensors, IMUs, encoders, and vision/camera systems.
    • Wiring harness fabrication experience including building to a pinout, connector assembly, and cable routing on moving assemblies.
    • Background in a robotics research lab, hardware startup, aerospace, or advanced electromechanical environment where rapid prototyping and tight engineering collaboration are standard.
    • Mechatronics training/coursework or electromechanical troubleshooting experience.
    • Some scripting ability (Python or bash) for test and calibration; basic familiarity with git, Docker, or networking.
    • Experience with ERP systems, MES, PLM, or lab management tools for tracking inventory, build status, component traceability, and hardware/software revision control.
Work Environment & Physical Requirements

    • On-site lab role; standing, bench work, and hands-on assembly for extended periods, including work in awkward positions and tight spaces.
    • Fine motor precision and close-vision work with small fasteners, connectors, and board-level components.
    • Lifting and maneuvering heavy robotic assemblies; use of required PPE.
    • Work around high-voltage electronics, powered actuators, and moving machinery.

Salary Range

    • $90,000-$105,000
    • The actual salary offered is dependent on various factors including, but not limited to, location, the candidate’s combination of job-related knowledge, qualifications, skills, education, training, and experience

new_jobs.description:
Join the Future of Robotic Biomanufacturing!

Multiply Labs
is a robotics company on a mission to solve a significant bottleneck in modern medicine: the manufacturing of life-saving advanced biologics, from gene and cell therapies to antibodies and more.

Today, these therapies are produced through manual, labor-intensive processes. Costs are extremely high—often $500K-$2M per patient—limiting access to only a small fraction of those who need them.

As product complexity increases and the cost of failure and scientific labor rises, the industry is shifting toward automation. Robotics and AI are making automated biologics manufacturing feasible, reliable, and economically scalable.

We believe the future of biomanufacturing is robotic—closed, automated, and scalable—ensuring critical therapeutics are accessible to every patient who needs them.

Why This Matters

We don’t just build robots—we’re building the essential infrastructure for next generation biologics. Our technology enables biopharma companies to scale production without redesigning their science, reducing regulatory hurdles and lowering costs so these treatments can reach more patients.

The Stack & The Scale

The Mission: Build the world’s best robots to make life-saving therapies accessible to all.
The Technology: Advanced robotic orchestration, high-precision automation, cloud-integrated hardware-software systems, dextrous manipulation, and imitation learning.
The Location: Headquartered in San Francisco, CA.
The Backing: Supported by premier investors, including Casdin Capital, Lux Capital, and Y Combinator.

To learn more and to view a video of our robots in action, visit us at www.multiplylabs.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

About The Role

We are seeking a highly skilled, hands-on R&D Lab & Shop Manager to lead daily operations across our prototyping lab, machine shop, and assembly areas. In this role, you will bridge the gap between design engineering and physical hardware execution, managing machine shop equipment, maintaining additive manufacturing systems, executing precision mechanical assemblies, and collaborating with cross-functional engineering teams on Design for Manufacturability/Assembly (DFM/DFA).

Responsibilities

Lab & Shop Operations: Oversee daily lab safety, 5S organization, tool tracking, and OSHA compliance; maintain equipment calibration logs and maintenance records for ISO 13485/FDA quality standards.
Machining & Metal Fabrication: Operate vertical mills, saws, hand tools and other metal working equipment
Precision Mechanical Assembly: Build complex electro-mechanical assemblies, sub-systems, and robotic end-effectors according to technical engineering drawings, schematics, & BOMs
Engineering Collaboration & DFM: Partner directly with design engineers to debug fit/tolerance issues, provide DFM/DFA feedback on early prototypes
Logistics & Receiving: Open and organize incoming shipments, organize inventory

Qualifications

5+ years of hands-on experience in a machine shop, R&D lab, or rapid prototyping environment within the robotics or medical device industry.
Working experience in GD&T, technical schematics, exploded diagrams, and precision measurement tools (calipers, micrometers, height gauges, dial indicators).

Additional preferred qualifications:

Hands-on expertise in operating, maintaining, and post-processing FDM and SLA/resin printing platforms

Nice to Haves

Forklift Certification a plus

Physical & Working Conditions

Lift 50 lbs

Total Rewards & Life at Multiply Labs

Competitive Compensation: Salary range of $45 - $50/hr plus meaningful early-stage equity. We want our team to have a real stake in the future we’re building.
Premium Health: Premium Medical, Dental, and Vision plans with subsidies for child dependents.
Wealth Building: 401(k) with a 4% company match to help you plan for the long term.
Pre-Tax Commuter Benefit. Pay for eligible transit and parking with pre-tax dollars to save on commuting costs.
Parental Support: Robust Paid Parental Leave to support your family’s newest additions.
True Flexibility: We offer Flexible PTO and 12 Paid Holidays, trusting you to manage your time and recharge when you need it.
No Set Hours: Set your own schedule in alignment with your manager and team. We hold a high bar, measuring success by impact and outcomes - not hours logged.
Office Perks: A vibrant SF office culture featuring catered team lunches, stocked kitchen, and frequent team events.
H-1B and Green Card sponsorship available for exceptional talent.
Referral bonuses for helping us build a world-class team.
Great people, meaningful work, and a team that genuinely believes in what we're building.

Come build the world’s best robots—and help make life-saving therapies accessible to all.

We actively seek candidates with diverse perspectives and lived experiences. We’re committed to building a team where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered to do their best work.

Multiply Labs encourages candidates from all backgrounds to apply — even if you don’t meet every qualification. If you’re excited about our mission and think you can contribute, we’d love to hear from you.

new_jobs.title: Clinical Research Associate
new_jobs.description:
Lycia Therapeutics (Nasdaq: LYCA) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company using its proprietary lysosomal targeting chimera (LYTAC) platform to discover and develop therapeutics that degrade extracellular and membrane-bound proteins. These proteins drive a wide range of difficult-to-treat diseases, including autoimmune, inflammatory, and allergic conditions. Lycia was established in 2019 in collaboration with academic founder and Nobel Laureate Carolyn Bertozzi, Ph.D., professor of chemistry and HHMI investigator at Stanford University. In October 2026, Lycia completed an initial public offering, and its common stock now trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “LYCA.” Lycia is headquartered in South San Francisco.

Visit https://lyciatx.com/ for more information.

The Role:

The Clinical Research Associate is responsible for monitoring clinical trial sites to ensure that studies are conducted ethically, safely, and in full compliance with the trial protocol, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines, and applicable regulatory requirements. The CRA will act as the primary bridge between Lycia and the clinical research sites.

Key Responsibilities

In-house

Site Management and Support: Assist with investigator recruitment, site selection activities, study startup, and close-out tasks. Provide ongoing operational support to investigative sites via phone and email
Document & Regulatory Tracking: Collect, review, and track essential regulatory documents and Investigator Site Files (ISF) to ensure audit and inspection readiness. Maintain the electronic Trial Master File (eTMF)
Data and Query Management: Review data points and findings within Electronic Data Capture (EDC) systems. Write, track, and follow up on clinical data queries with site personnel
Remote Monitoring & Collaboration: Support traveling CRAs by conducting remote monitoring activities, tracking site key performance indicators (KPIs), and updating Clinical Trial Management Systems (CTMS)
Compliance & Escalation: Ensure trial conduct aligns with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines, FDA/local regulations, and study-specific standard operating procedures (SOPs). Escalate site non-compliance or protocol deviations to Clinical Operations Management

Clinical Research Site Oversight

Site Monitoring Visits: Conduct qualification, site initiation, interim monitoring, and close-out visits in person or via remote monitoring tools
Data Verification: Review source documents, medical records, and Case Report Forms (CRFs/EDC) to verify data accuracy, completeness, and integrity
Protocol & Regulatory Compliance: Ensure site staff adhere to the study protocol, ICH-GCP guidelines, FDA regulations, and standard operating procedures (SOPs)
Issue Escalation: Identify, document, and track protocol deviations, adverse events, and data queries, working with site investigators to implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA)
Investigational Product (IP) Management: Check accountability, storage, dispensing, and return of investigational drugs or devices at study sites
Documentation & Reporting: Maintain comprehensive Trial Master File (TMF) documents and write detailed monitoring visit reports (trip reports) within required timelines
Site Support & Training: Train investigators and clinical research coordinators (CRCs) on study protocols, electronic data capture systems, and regulatory requirements

Required Qualifications & Skills

Education: Bachelor’s or advanced degree in a life science, nursing, pharmacy, or health-related field
Experience: 2+ years of clinical research experience (e.g., prior experience as a Clinical Research Coordinator, clinical data assistant, or junior CRA)
Regulatory Knowledge: Deep understanding of ICH-GCP guidelines, FDA regulations, EU, and local ethics/IRB processes
Technical Skills: Proficiency with Electronic Data Capture (EDC) systems, Clinical Trial Management Systems (CTMS), and remote data review tools
Core Competencies:
Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills
Effective verbal and written communication
High level of organization and time management

new_jobs.title: Research Scientist I, Attribute Sciences Computational Biology, AI & Scientific Informatics
new_jobs.description:
We’re here for one reason and one reason only – to cure cancer. Every moment is dedicated to developing treatments and every action moves us one step closer to our goal. We’ve made incredible scientific breakthroughs and our pioneering personalized CAR T-cell therapies have changed the paradigm. But we're not finished yet.

Join Kite, as we make even bigger advances in cancer therapies, and help shape where our business and medical science goes next.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfill their aspirations. Join Kite and help create more tomorrows.

Job Description

The Research Scientist I, Attribute Sciences Computational Biology, AI & Scientific Informatics will be responsible for accelerating adoption of artificial intelligence, agentic workflows, and advanced analytics across Analytical Development. This role will combine expertise in biological sciences, bioinformatics, data science, and generative AI to build AI-powered tools that improve scientific productivity, knowledge management, data accessibility, and decision-making to guide process development and product knowledge of viral vector-based gene delivery platforms and T cell therapies. In this role, the research scientist will partner closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Manufacturing Sciences, Digital/IT, and Data Science teams to develop AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, workflow automations, and predictive models that leverage laboratory, process, and knowledge-management data. Ideal candidates would possess strong communications skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, curiosity about emerging AI capabilities, ability to understand scientific workflows and needs and translate those into working products, and software/programming skills sufficient to independently build and deploy AI and data science solutions.

Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

AI Agent Development:

Design and deploy Copilot, Copilot Studio, or similar AI agents supporting scientific workflows.
Develop RAG-based knowledge assistants that integrate information from various enterprise knowledge sources.
Create agents that: answer scientific questions, retrieve and summarize technical information, generate draft reports, support investigations, assist with study planning and scheduling, support operational excellence.
Evaluate AI tool accuracy, groundedness, hallucination rates, performance and citation quality.

Bioinformatics & Scientific Computing

Analyze multi-modal biological datasets including NGS, omics, vector characterization, cell therapy process data.
Develop pipelines for automated data processing and visualization.

Knowledge Management and Automation

Support digital transformation initiatives involving electronic lab notebook and data lake infrastructure.
Automate repetitive scientific workflows and documentation tasks.
Build solutions that improve data discoverability and scientific knowledge reuse.

Cross-functional Collaboration

Work directly with scientists, IT and digital teams to identify opportunities where AI can improve productivity.
Translate scientific business problems into technical AI solutions.
Train stakeholders on effective use of AI tools and prompt engineering techniques.

Applied Data Science

Build predictive and descriptive models supporting process development and manufacturing.
Develop statistical tools for identifying relationships between process parameters and manufacturing outcomes.
Design dashboards and decision-support systems.

Basic Qualifications

Ph.D. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Data Science, Computer Science or related discipline OR
Masters' Degree and 4+ years experience; OR
Bachelor's Degree and 6+ years experience; OR
Associates Degree and 8+ years experience; OR
High School Degree and 10+year experience

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of experience in AI, including experience with LLMs, vector databases, agentic frameworks, prompt engineering, and evaluation frameworks.
Knowledge of advanced statistical techniques/concepts and proficiency in statistical computer languages (i.e. R, Python, SQL) to analyze data and draw insights from large data sets.
Knowledge of cell biology, cancer biology, and/or immunology.
Experience performing bioinformatics (NGS analysis) and/or data analytics with high dimensional data to drive business solutions.
Experience with machine learning, statistical modeling, experimental design and data visualization.
Ability to think critically and demonstrate troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
Highly collaborative with excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills
Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and willing to accept temporary responsibilities outside of initial job description
Comfortable in a dynamic, fast-paced environment

The salary range for this position is: $133,195.00 - $172,370.00. Kite considers a variety of factors when determining base compensation, including experience, qualifications, and geographic location. These considerations mean actual compensation will vary. This position may also be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus, discretionary stock-based long-term incentives (eligibility may vary based on role), paid time off, and a benefits package. new_jobs.title: Korean Voice AI Evaluator – Native Speakers Wanted
new_jobs.description:
Korean Voice AI Evaluator (Healthcare Front Desk Conversations)

About The Role

What if your voice could help teach AI how to handle a real phone call to a hospital or clinic? We're looking for native Korean speakers based in the United States to hold natural spoken conversations with an AI healthcare receptionist, then evaluate how well it listens, responds, and takes action.

With one of the largest Korean-speaking diaspora communities in the world, the US is home to a wealth of native-fluency talent perfectly suited to this role. You'll role-play as a patient using fictional personas we provide, record short conversations, and grade the AI's performance — all from home, on your own schedule.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Contract (task-based)
Location: Remote
Commitment: Flexible, work at your own pace

What You'll Do

Hold 4 to 5 minute spoken conversations in Korean with an AI front desk assistant, playing a fictional patient
Say natural trigger phrases to test whether the AI makes the correct function calls — for example, checking a patient record, booking an appointment, or checking insurance
Review transcripts and classify how accurately the AI understood you and responded
Flag issues such as mispronunciations, cutoffs, interruptions, delays, and incorrect function calls, including timestamps
Test how the AI handles background noise, short replies ("네," "아니요," "괜찮아요"), long numbers, emotional moments, and sensitive or unsafe requests
Follow detailed labeling guidelines consistently and submit high-quality work

Who You Are

Native or near-native Korean speaker with a clear, natural speaking voice
Detail-oriented, with the patience to review recordings and transcripts closely
Comfortable role-playing a patient and sounding authentic
Able to follow multi-step instructions and apply them consistently
Reliable and self-directed when working independently

new_jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff: Python, TypeScript & LLM Agent Evals | San Francisco On-site | Up to $400K + Equity
new_jobs.description:
"Good morning! And in case I don't see ya..." Truman Burbank, The Truman Show

Every AI agent thinks it lives in a perfect little world. Clean prompts, polite users, happy paths only. Sunny Seahaven, every day.

Your job is to sail out to the horizon and find where the sky is painted on.

THE OPPORTUNITY

A well-funded, seed-stage San Francisco startup is building the trust layer for AI agents, making sure they're safe and reliable before they're handed real responsibility in high-stakes industries. It's backed by top-tier AI investors, and the team is small, senior and stacked with people who have built companies before.

These agents are already in production at some of the most widely used AI products on the planet. Somebody has to find out how they break before the real world does. That's you.

This is a senior individual contributor seat with a rare mix: hardcore engineering, frontier AI research turned into product, and real contact with the customer teams building the agents everyone uses.

WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO

Own red-team engagements end to end on major customers' agents: scoping, recon, attack execution, remediation and sign-off
Sharpen the core engine that powers every evaluation the company runs
Turn bleeding-edge adversarial research into repeatable product
Be the palate for eval quality. If a test is weak, you send it back to the kitchen
Automate your own workflow with agents, because doing it twice by hand is a crime
Work out how to test the next wave, like computer-use agents, before anyone has a playbook for them

THE TECH YOU'LL LIVE IN

Python is the engine room.
Evals, attack pipelines and grading logic all run here, so you'll write production-grade Python fluently. That means async code that fires thousands of conversations at an agent in parallel, clean typed data models, solid tests, and the judgment to know when a script needs to grow up into a system.

TypeScript is where the work meets people.
Customers need to see results, findings and reports, and you'll ship that user-facing side yourself. If you're strong in React and Node, typed end to end and built with the same care as the backend, you'll feel at home. This one is non-negotiable: they want engineers who already write both languages well, not people planning to learn one.

LLMs and agents are your raw material.
You should be comfortable with the major model APIs, tool and function calling, structured outputs, retrieval, multi-turn agent loops, and protocols like MCP that connect agents to the outside world. Hands-on time with agent frameworks and orchestration is a big plus.

Evals are the craft.
Designing test suites that actually catch failures. Using LLM-as-judge grading without fooling yourself. Building golden datasets, generating synthetic adversarial scenarios at scale, and proving whether a fix really worked or just moved the problem somewhere else.

Adversarial AI is the fun bit.
Prompt injection, jailbreaks, tool misuse, data leakage, harmful outputs, and agents going off-script under multi-turn pressure. If you've read the latest red-teaming papers and itched to try them on a real production system, this is the job.

Integration is the glue.
Every customer's agent is different, so you'll work across SDKs, API endpoints, webhooks and the occasional ugly legacy system, often getting a new integration running in days. Browser automation and computer-use tooling will matter more and more as agents start clicking around the web on their own.

MUST HAVE

Real production experience shipping user-facing features, not just backend plumbing
Strong, hands-on Python and TypeScript. Both, not "happy to pick it up"
5+ years as a software engineer, owning high-stakes technical work from start to finish
A career arc that keeps climbing in title and scope
A CS degree or equivalent technical background
Agentic AI tools baked into how you work every day
Clear communication with engineers and non-technical stakeholders alike
On-site in San Francisco, 5 days a week

BONUS POINTS

Founder, founding engineer or early startup hire (extra credit if it was VC-backed)
Customer-facing experience
Hands-on with agentic frameworks and evals
A visible spike: a side project people talk about, open source, writing, a standout company, or a bold career move that shows real conviction

PROBABLY NOT FOR YOU IF

Your whole career has been at big tech with no early-stage time
You're an engineering manager who's drifted away from writing code
You're after a management or director title. This is a senior IC seat, and that's the point

WHY THIS ONE IS WORTH YOUR TIME

You'll work on one of the biggest open problems in AI: knowing whether an agent can be trusted before it does something that matters
Your work lands in production with customers whose agents are used by millions
Small team, huge surface area, and a direct line to the founders
The category is brand new, so the playbook you write could become the industry standard

THE PACKAGE

Up to $400K base + meaningful equity
On-site in SF with a small, sharp, very senior team
Visa transfers welcome (OPT, H-1B transfers)
A quick, focused process: a short vibe check, a coding round, then an onsite covering systems design, algorithms and a deep-dive on AI evals

HOW TO APPLY

Hit apply with your resume and answer the screening questions. Big Wave Digital is recruiting this role on behalf of our client, and every application is read by a real person.

"We accept the reality of the world with which we're presented." Christof, The Truman Show

The agents accept it. You won't.

new_jobs.title: AI Scientist, Agentic CAD (AI4Engineering)
new_jobs.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

You will join the AI4Engineering Science team, the Mistral research group that builds the data and evaluation infrastructure and owns the SFT/RL processes for AI4Engineering that teach our frontier LLMs to do real engineering work. The agentic engineering group works alongside the Physics AI research in the wider Science organisation.

This seat sits in the agentic CAD stream. Together with the Solutions and Applied teams, the group carries this work into customer projects with industrial partners in automotive, aerospace, semiconductors, and beyond.

The Role

Mistral is looking for an AI Scientist with deep machine learning expertise and hands-on CAD experience to expand what our agentic tools can do for computer-aided design. Your focus is a single mission: teaching Mistral's LLMs to generate, analyze, and modify CAD designs the way an expert design engineer would.

Your core work is building the pre- and post-training data for Mistral's LLMs to reason about and execute real CAD tasks: text-to-CAD and image-to-CAD generation from technical drawings, geometric analysis and QA of CAD parts, and modification of existing designs. Because Mistral trains its own frontier LLMs, the data and verifiers you design ship directly into models you can hold - a rare position, and the core of the job.

Alongside this, you will help shape the agent architectures and harnesses that let these models operate reliably inside multi-step CAD workflows, driving CAD tools through APIs or computer use across the whole design loop.

This is early-stage work, and that's the point: you are joining at the foundation, shaping the data, verifiers, and agent scaffolding that decide whether these systems become reliable or stay demo-grade. There is no inherited playbook; you will help define what good looks like, and your work will set the direction the CAD stream builds on rather than extend an existing one.

What You Will Do

Design pretraining, SFT, and RL data for CAD tasks: text-to-CAD and image-to-CAD generation from technical drawings, geometric analysis and QA of CAD parts, and design modification
Define verifiers and evaluation criteria that capture what "correct" and "high-quality" actually mean for CAD tasks
Scale the data pipelines that produce agentic CAD training traces
Design and improve agent architectures and harnesses: how models plan, call CAD tools via API or computer use, recover from errors, and chain steps together across long-horizon design workflows
Build and maintain CAD evaluation benchmarks and diagnostic tooling, from parametric CAD and drawing-to-3D benchmarks to industrial evaluations, identifying where models fail and tracing those failures back to gaps in data, reward design, or agent scaffolding
Collaborate with CAD domain experts and the CAE and EDA streams (and the science and solutions teams more broadly) to identify which CAD workflows are highest-value to target next
Contribute to Mistral's broader pre- and post-training research, sharing findings and methodology across the science organization

What We're Looking For

Deep, hands-on machine learning expertise, particularly LLM development: you have built LLM training pipelines (SFT, RL, fine-tuning, GRPO), demonstrated in publications or shipped systems rather than CV claims
Demonstrated hands-on CAD experience: you have designed, scripted, or automated real CAD workflows in tools such as SolidWorks, CATIA, Siemens NX, FreeCAD, or CADQuery, ideally with CAD-kernel grounding (OpenCASCADE, build123d)
Fluent English with excellent communication skills: you can explain technical ML and CAD concepts to both engineering and non-technical audiences
You write clean, readable Python code and are comfortable in Linux/HPC environments
Self-directed: you do not need detailed roadmaps to make progress
Low-ego, collaborative, and eager to learn at the intersection of CAD and ML

It would be great if you:

Have experience building or fine-tuning agentic systems (tool use, multi-step planning, agent orchestration frameworks)
Have experience with reward modeling, RLHF/RLAIF/RLVR, or preference-based training
Have first-author publications or open-source benchmark work in agentic CAD or CAD-ML, such as CAD generation benchmarks or RL/GRPO fine-tuning of vision-language models for CAD
Have contributed to a large open-source or industry codebase
Have publications in engineering and ML venues (NeurIPS, ICLR, ICCV, SIGGRAPH, JFM, AIAA, etc.)

What we offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

new_jobs.title: Applied AI Architect, Beneficial Deployments (Life Sciences Community & Enablement)
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Beneficial Deployments

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.

About The Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Architect to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team, focused on helping scientists everywhere get the most from Claude, especially Claude Science. You'll run enablements, workshops and hackathons, build demos that show what frontier models can do for the field, and grow a community of scientists building with Claude. You'll also scale scientific enablement inside Anthropic, so our Applied AI and customer teams can support scientists without you in the room.

Responsibilities

Be the DRI for scientific enablement: decide what to run, build the materials, deliver them, and measure whether research teams reach daily use of Claude.
Lead our programs for activating scientists at scale, such as LSVP and Claude for Researchers: set the goals, design the program and run it.
Build demos, notebooks and tutorials that show scientists what frontier models can do in their own work, and be an active voice where scientists share tools online (X, LinkedIn, etc.).
Scale scientific enablement inside Anthropic: train our Applied AI and Customer Success teams, and build playbooks they can run without you.
Build and lead a scientist community around Claude, and be its ambassador (and support ambassador programs), from small meetups to large conferences.
Be the voice of scientists inside Anthropic: turn what you hear into concrete asks and see them through to launch, and partner with Marketing and Comms so campaigns and content reach the scientific community.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have

Deep hands-on expertise with AI tools for science such as Claude Science: you know where they shine and where they break.
Real credibility as a scientist: hands-on experience doing science in academic labs, biotechs, pharma or research institutes, ideally as a user of the kind of tools you'll help scientists adopt. Experience building or running programs for scientific communities is a plus.
A track record of helping many scientific teams adopt a new tool through demos, trainings, workshops or hackathons.
Up to date on AI for science, such as agentic analysis and AI co-scientists, and able to explain it to working scientists.
Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs: you can prototype a working demo. You don't need to write production code.
Clear written and spoken communication: talks, tutorials and docs that scientists find useful.
A track record of taking programs or products from idea to results: you set the direction, did the work and were accountable for the outcome, often with no playbook.
Comfort operating in ambiguity: you bring clarity to fuzzy problems, wear multiple hats and do whatever it takes to further the mission.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$275,000—$315,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

The Department of Integrative Biology at the University of South Florida (USF), Tampa invites applications for a Computational Biologist to fill a 9-month, full-time and tenure-earning, Assistant Professor position, with an appointment start date of August 7, 2027. Salary is negotiable.

We encourage applicants conducting ecological, evolutionary, or behavioral research with statistical, computational, or theoretical approaches. This includes, but is not limited to, biological/ecological data science, bioinformatics, biostatistics, -omics, machine learning/deep learning, and research at scales ranging from genes to ecosystems. Interdisciplinary approaches are encouraged.

USF offers opportunities for collaboration across campus with programs in mathematics, the College of Engineering, the Bellini College of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity and Computing, and the College of Marine Science. USF also hosts two high-performance computing clusters and an interdisciplinary Genomics Program in the College of Public Health. Local agency partners in the Tampa Bay area include FWRI, USGS, NOAA, and USFWS.

Responsibilities

Candidates are expected to establish a strong, externally funded research program and to teach and develop quantitative courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Examples include statistical ecology, biometry, Bayesian statistics, mathematical modeling, bioinformatics, and data science for biologists.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:
Ph.D. in Computer Science, Ecology, Evolutionary Biology, Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, or a related field from an accredited institution, publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals, and experience teaching undergraduate or graduate students. Must meet university criteria for appointment to the rank of Assistant Professor.

Preferred Qualifications:
Post-doctoral training in a relevant field, procurement of research funding, and demonstration of success with teaching upper-level quantitative courses and mentoring students of all backgrounds.

How To Apply-

Please submit the following application materials as a single combined PDF document -

Cover letter
CV
Statement of current and future research directions, up to two to three pages long, including a strategy for establishing an independent, externally funded research program
Teaching statement one to two pages long, describing teaching experience and approach
Up to three selected publications or data/software products
Names and contact information of at least three references

Redefining Healthcare with AI

Xsolis is an AI-driven technology company reducing administrative waste in healthcare by enabling smarter collaboration between providers and payers. Since 2013, our vision has been to create a frictionless healthcare system.

Our flagship product, Dragonfly®, is the first and only AI-driven platform to continuously assign real-time predictive scores for medical necessity. Dragonfly has delivered proven results across 600+ hospital, health system, and health plan clients and earned repeated industry recognition. With recognition on the Inc. 5000  and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 lists, Xsolis is also one of the fastest-growing privately-held companies in the country and across North America, and we're looking for talented people to grow with us.

Position Summary Details

Xsolis is hiring a Senior Manager, Data Science to set the vision for how we use predictive, generative and agentic AI, and to build and lead the team that delivers it. You will spot the opportunities worth pursuing, shape them into a strategy, and take them from idea to production.

This is a leadership role with expectation on deep hands-on coding knowledge. We want a self-starter who doesn't wait for a roadmap: someone who can take a rough idea, rally a team around it and run with it. You will have the technical depth to guide decisions on model training, LLM fine-tuning and agent design, and you will spend your time leading people and driving outcomes in partnership with product and engineering teams

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

The essential functions include, but are not limited to the following:

Vision and strategy

Define a multi-year vision and roadmap for data science, ML and agentic AI, tied to business goals.
Identify where AI creates the most value and make the case to leadership for where to invest.
Track where the field is heading (LLMs, agents, fine-tuning) and decide what the team adopts, and when.

Taking ideas from zero to one

Take loosely defined ideas and turn them into scoped bets with clear goals, milestones and success metrics.
Move quickly from concept to prototype to production without waiting for a fully formed plan.
Own outcomes end to end, and know when to push forward, pivot or stop.

Team leadership

Build, hire and grow a high-performing team of data scientists and ML engineers.
Mentor through regular 1:1s, career plans and honest feedback, and develop future leaders on the team.
Create a culture of ownership, experimentation and high standards.
Delegate the technical work and empower the team to make decisions.

Technical direction: models and LLMs

Set standards and review designs for training deep learning models, including GPU and distributed training (data, model and pipeline parallelism).
Guide LLM strategy: when to prompt, use RAG, or fine-tune with PEFT methods such as LoRA and QLoRA.
Make sure models are evaluated rigorously before and after they ship, and that GPU spend stays under control.

Technical direction: agentic AI and infrastructure

Shape the architecture for agentic systems on AWS: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, SageMaker, Lambda, EventBridge and ECS, with CloudWatch for observability.
Champion MLOps practices: Docker, infrastructure as code with Terraform, CI/CD for models and production monitoring.
Set guardrails for safe, responsible AI: agent permissions, data privacy and human review.

Stakeholders and delivery

Partner regularly with product, data engineering and platform leaders to align on priorities and roadmap.
Communicate vision, trade-offs and results clearly to executives and non-technical audiences.
Run the team in an agile cadence (sprint planning, backlog prioritization, retros) with predictable delivery.

Strong understanding on practical deployment of agents to production using Agentcore and aligning with the organization’s agentic AI roadmap.
A self-starter who thrives in ambiguity and drives initiatives without needing detailed direction.
Deep understanding of deep learning and GPU training at scale, including distributed training, enough to guide the team and challenge its decisions.
Strong grasp of LLM fine-tuning (PEFT, LoRA, QLoRA) and agentic AI architecture.
Familiarity with AWS ML and serverless services (SageMaker, Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda, EventBridge, ECS), Docker and Terraform.
Experience leading agile teams and managing projects across several stakeholder groups.
An excellent communicator who can influence product, engineering and executive stakeholders.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, statistics, math or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience presenting strategy to executive leadership
Master's or PhD in a quantitative field.

Experience owning cloud and GPU budgets.

new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Team

Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a world-class research group focused on making fundamental biological discoveries. The team combines cutting-edge AI with hands-on biological research, positioning Anthropic at the forefront of AI-accelerated scientific discovery.

About The Role

We're seeking an exceptional Research Scientist to join the team. This role combines deep computational biology expertise with frontier AI capabilities, positioning Anthropic at the forefront of AI-driven scientific discovery.

As one of the first computational members of this Life Sciences research group, you'll work on a high-impact team that operates at the intersection of computational and experimental biology. You'll bring broad computational biology experience to bear across the team's projects, driving discoveries from large-scale computational analysis of biological data through to results our experimental scientists can test, and moving flexibly between problems as the science demands. You'll have substantial access to Claude and you'll help establish how computational biology operates at Anthropic.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape how AI transforms biological research. You'll work with some of the world's best AI researchers while tackling problems that matter deeply for scientific understanding and biomedicine. If you're excited about using your computational expertise to make fundamental biological discoveries and guide the development of transformative AI systems, we want to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

Build, run, and maintain the analysis pipelines that back the team's experimental programs: sequence analysis at petabyte scale, structural bioinformatics, phylogenetic and comparative genomics, design and analysis of high-throughput functional screens, biological sequence modeling, etc.
Partner directly with experimental biologists to design experiments that produce high-quality data, and turn results around fast enough to immediately inform the next experiment
Draw on the literature and curated biological knowledge bases alongside primary data to generate and prioritize hypotheses for experimental follow-up
Stand up and maintain the team's computational infrastructure: data ingestion, workflow orchestration, internal databases, and the interfaces that make all of it accessible to both researchers and AI agents
Use Claude and our internal agent frameworks heavily in your own work, and feed what you learn back to the model-improvement and product teams as evaluations, datasets, and concrete failure cases
Pick up analyses across projects as priorities shift; we're looking for breadth and flexibility over a single deep specialty

Minimum Qualifications

Have a PhD in computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, biophysics, machine learning, computer science, or a related quantitative or biological field, or equivalent industry research experience
Have a track record of computational biology research you have led end to end, from question to result, with evidence of impact (for example publications, preprints, released datasets or tools, or research that changed a program's direction)
Have demonstrated breadth across multiple areas of computational biology
Are proficient in one or more programming languages used in scientific computing and comfortable working on large datasets in Linux and cloud compute environments
Can take an ambiguous biological question, scope the analysis, and produce a result an experimentalist can act on
Communicate computational results clearly to both biologists and ML researchers

Preferred Qualifications

Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and developing solutions in rapidly evolving research environments
Are results-oriented, with a bias towards flexibility and impact
Hands-on experience in experimental biology, or a track record of designing experiments side by side with experimentalists
Experience building tools, pipelines, or agentic systems on top of LLMs, or training models on biological sequence data
Deep expertise in one or two areas of computational biology (for example structural biology, metagenomics, single-cell genomics, or protein design) on top of the required breadth

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$300,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.

The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time.

What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.

This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain biology software in genomics and structural biology (libraries, command-line tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks) for use by researchers and AI agents, inside Anthropic and externally
Own the path from research code to public release, including testing, validation against reference data and established tools, benchmarking, documentation, and packaging, and make the call on when something is ready to ship
Maintain what we release: triage issues, review outside contributions, and manage breaking changes
Represent the team in the biology community through conferences, workshops, tutorials, and direct work with researchers and maintainers, and turn what you learn about their needs into priorities for the team
Partner with the team's computational and experimental scientists to turn research code into well-tested, reusable software
Lead the technical direction of the projects you own through design review, code review, and mentoring, and, depending on your interests and the team's needs, lead a small team
Build with Claude and AI coding agents as your default way of working, hold agent-written code to the same standard as your own, and set the team's practices for reviewing and validating it

Minimum Qualifications

Practice rigorous testing and release engineering: unit and integration tests, continuous integration, validation against reference data, packaging, and versioning
Use AI coding tools as a central part of how you build software, and can show how you verify the correctness and performance of code you did not write by hand

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About The Role

As an Applied AI Engineer on the Startups team at Anthropic, you will be a trusted technical advisor to the top AI-native life sciences and biotech startups as they grow from early product to scale. Some of these companies build products on Claude that they sell to the rest of the industry, and others do the science themselves and want Claude woven into how their own research runs, and this role works with both. You'll lead deep technical engagements, partnering directly with startup engineering and scientific teams to help them build their products on Claude and run their own research with it, advising on implementation and agent design as they build what is newly possible with AI in the life sciences. You will bridge the gap between what Claude can do and what the life sciences need, working alongside some of the strongest teams in the field on problems that matter and pushing the boundaries of AI in science as you go.

Working closely with Applied AI Architects, Account Executives, and Anthropic's Product, Engineering, and Research teams, you'll help startups build at the edge of what is possible with Claude. You'll leverage your AI engineering expertise and your scientific domain knowledge to develop custom evaluation frameworks, design scalable architectures, and create the technical resources that enable life sciences startups to succeed with Claude.

Serve as a deep technical advisor to high-potential life sciences and biotech startups, whether Claude sits inside the product they sell or inside the way they make discoveries, working alongside them to build innovative use cases that push the boundaries of AI in scientific research and development
Work hands-on with startup engineering teams and their scientists through pair programming and architecture reviews that accelerate their development, and understand their scientific workflows end to end so that your guidance fits into real research pipelines
Develop prototypes and technical documentation, including evaluation suites, scientifically grounded benchmarks, AI engineering techniques, and architecture diagrams, that enable startups to build, operate, and scale with Claude
Create reference implementations and sample code that many companies can adopt without starting from scratch, such as example MCP servers for domain-specific data sources like genomics platforms, literature databases, and experimental repositories, along with agent skills for common scientific workflows

We’re here for one reason and one reason only – to cure cancer. Every moment is dedicated to developing treatments and every action moves us one step closer to our goal. We’ve made incredible scientific breakthroughs and our pioneering personalized CAR T-cell therapies have changed the paradigm. But we're not finished yet.

Join Kite, as we make even bigger advances in cancer therapies, and help shape where our business and medical science goes next.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfill their aspirations. Join Kite and help create more tomorrows.

Job Description

The Research Scientist I, Attribute Sciences Computational Biology, AI & Scientific Informatics will be responsible for accelerating adoption of artificial intelligence, agentic workflows, and advanced analytics across Analytical Development. This role will combine expertise in biological sciences, bioinformatics, data science, and generative AI to build AI-powered tools that improve scientific productivity, knowledge management, data accessibility, and decision-making to guide process development and product knowledge of viral vector-based gene delivery platforms and T cell therapies. In this role, the research scientist will partner closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Manufacturing Sciences, Digital/IT, and Data Science teams to develop AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, workflow automations, and predictive models that leverage laboratory, process, and knowledge-management data. Ideal candidates would possess strong communications skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, curiosity about emerging AI capabilities, ability to understand scientific workflows and needs and translate those into working products, and software/programming skills sufficient to independently build and deploy AI and data science solutions.

AI Agent Development

Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

Design and deploy Copilot, Copilot Studio, or similar AI agents supporting scientific workflows.
Develop RAG-based knowledge assistants that integrate information from various enterprise knowledge sources.
Create agents that: answer scientific questions, retrieve and summarize technical information, generate draft reports, support investigations, assist with study planning and scheduling, support operational excellence.
Evaluate AI tool accuracy, groundedness, hallucination rates, performance and citation quality.

Bioinformatics & Scientific Computing

Analyze multi-modal biological datasets including NGS, omics, vector characterization, cell therapy process data.
Develop pipelines for automated data processing and visualization.

Knowledge Management and Automation

Support digital transformation initiatives involving electronic lab notebook and data lake infrastructure.
Automate repetitive scientific workflows and documentation tasks.
Build solutions that improve data discoverability and scientific knowledge reuse.

Cross-functional Collaboration

Work directly with scientists, IT and digital teams to identify opportunities where AI can improve productivity.
Translate scientific business problems into technical AI solutions.
Train stakeholders on effective use of AI tools and prompt engineering techniques.

Applied Data Science

Build predictive and descriptive models supporting process development and manufacturing.
Develop statistical tools for identifying relationships between process parameters and manufacturing outcomes.
Design dashboards and decision-support systems.

Basic Qualifications

Ph.D. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Data Science, Computer Science or related discipline OR
Masters' Degree and 4+ years experience; OR
Bachelor's Degree and 6+ years experience; OR
Associates Degree and 8+ years experience; OR
High School Degree and 10+year experience

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of experience in AI, including experience with LLMs, vector databases, agentic frameworks, prompt engineering, and evaluation frameworks.
Knowledge of advanced statistical techniques/concepts and proficiency in statistical computer languages (i.e. R, Python, SQL) to analyze data and draw insights from large data sets.
Knowledge of cell biology, cancer biology, and/or immunology.
Experience performing bioinformatics (NGS analysis) and/or data analytics with high dimensional data to drive business solutions.
Experience with machine learning, statistical modeling, experimental design and data visualization.
Ability to think critically and demonstrate troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
Highly collaborative with excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills
Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and willing to accept temporary responsibilities outside of initial job description
Comfortable in a dynamic, fast-paced environment

The salary range for this position is: $133,195.00 - $172,370.00. Kite considers a variety of factors when determining base compensation, including experience, qualifications, and geographic location. These considerations mean actual compensation will vary. This position may also be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus, discretionary stock-based long-term incentives (eligibility may vary based on role), paid time off, and a benefits package. Benefits include company-sponsored medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans*.

For Additional Benefits Information, Visit

https://www.gilead.com/careers/compensation-benefits-and-wellbeing

Plan the path from lead to IND-enabling studies, including in vivo pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, and the handoff to process development and manufacturing
Coordinate antibody production, characterization, and in vitro and in vivo studies with external contract research organizations and academic partners
Evaluate AI-designed antibodies, drive them to experimental readout, and feed results back to research teams
Ensure experimental data across programs is high quality and well documented, including sequences, protocols, raw data, and failure modes
Communicate findings clearly to biology, AI research, and life sciences audiences

Comfort navigating ambiguity and defining problems in a rapidly evolving research environment
